$comment: Files in src/app allowed to differ from apps/web/src (or to have no web counterpart). One entry per file or glob, relative to src/app. category: platform (a platform service is the reason), native-editor (the native editor is), desktop-only (a screen or tool web has no counterpart for). reason: why, in a sentence. Kit-API drift (onPress, testID, lists, dialogs) is never a reason: phase 4 removes it.

entries.reason: Assets (icons, illustrations, SVG and raster images) generated by tools/gen-assets.mjs, since the GPUI host cannot import asset files the way web's Vite build does.
Smoke screen that exercises every @platform service on the native host; web has no such screen.
Standalone status screen root.tsx shows for the boot/demo mode of the native host; web has no such screen.
Developer benchmarks for the native host (attachment I/O), not part of the app.
Actions the native editor asks its host for (links, attachments, previews); Tiptap does these inside the web editor.
Binds the native editor's host actions to the app's stores and attachment helpers; web's Tiptap editor has no host bridge.

Hosts the native editor (EditorSurface with its toolbar, host actions and plan permissions) where web mounts Tiptap with its DOM drop zone, scroll restore and search-result scrolling; saveContent, the tabs view, the download progress and the unlock view follow web's.

A heading is reached by asking the native editor to scroll to it (scrollToHeading); web scrolls the DOM node (scrollIntoViewById) and marks the headings in view from the editor's DOM scroll position, which the native editor does not expose.
Turns the plan's features into the command ids the native editor refuses (callout, outline and task lists, attachments, CSV tables); web's Tiptap editor checks them in its own permission handler.

Picked files come from @platform/files (PickedFile) and are hashed from their bytes with the platform's xxh64; web streams a DOM File into hashStream, reads image sizes with an element and queues with p-queue (not a desktop dependency, so a local queue with its API stands in).

Fullscreen goes through @platform windowControls (utils/fullscreen) instead of document.documentElement.requestFullscreen(), the selected-words note is a kit Text instead of a DOM <span>, and the zoom and statistics controls carry the test ids the desktop e2e specs find them by; sx values the kit cannot draw (fit-content, a raw box-shadow, !important) use the nearest tokens.

The kit's native text field is not a DOM textarea: it has no style.height or field-sizing to auto-grow, no selectionDirection, no instanceof HTMLTextAreaElement, no em font sizes or CSS font stacks, and preventDefault on Enter does not stop the newline, so the title is a controlled value that drops newlines and moves focus to the editor on Enter.
